metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent transposed B2:F5 to B8:E12. Marks in original: Clint=36, Olivia=83, Parah=35, Elijah=30. After sort descending by marks: Olivia(83), Clint(36), Parah(35), Elijah(30).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select ranges, paste-transpose, sort data ranges in LibreOffice Calc
metadata.explanation: Task chains transpose with a sort-by-marks-descending step. Evaluator checks header at B8 plus all 4 student rows in sorted order. Partial credit: 0.2 per row pair (name + marks). Initial state scores 0.0.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the xlsx file after postconfig saves it, extracting B8 (header) and B9:B12/E9:E12 (student names and marks) — the right cells for verifying both transpose and sort.
Metric correctly handles the type='rule' expected parameter: accesses rules dict directly via expected.get('B8', ...) without any incorrect .get('rules') or .get('type') patterns.
Expected values (Olivia=83, Clint=36, Parah=35, Elijah=30) correctly represent descending sort order and match the trajectory summary.
Partial credit scoring (0.2 per row, 0.1 per correct item within a row) is logically consistent with the multi-step task requiring both transpose and sort.
Negative control resistance is strong: initial state has B8 empty/not 'Student', so the evaluator will score 0.0 on an unsolved task.
Postconfig includes Ctrl+S to save the file before getter reads it, ensuring state freshness.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider also reading C8/D8 (Class/Subject header cells) to more fully verify the transposed table structure, though name+marks verification is sufficient for the sort check.
